purpose: Device-owned single-AIR cubic wallet proving with GPU periodic quotient evaluation and the unchanged wallet verifier/encoding
result: Eight fresh GPU-required release wallet proofs and four debug-compatible wallet proofs CPU-verified after GPU shutdown; strict wallet requests require all 15 applicable arithmetic stages
public_periodic_tables: Host copies/encodes static AIR literals; GPU interpolates/evaluates them as uncommitted quotient inputs. They do not change the proof transcript or verifier layout.
pilot_notes: Run 01 passed all runtime cases but the evidence verifier found that the invalid-wallet control disabled report output. Run 02 enables that control report and rebuilds/revalidates every profile.
Pilot 01 initialized only the witness engine and failed the full-pipeline admission check; the fixture was corrected to initialize the complete owned path.
Pilot 02 at 256 MiB managed GPU memory reached quotient commitment and returned GpuFailure with prior receipts retained. The device lease and all managed allocations released.
Pilot 03 at 1 GiB managed GPU memory passed two fresh GPU-required wallet proofs through CPU verification after GPU shutdown.
limitations: The new API is opt-in cubic research join-split proving; legacy quadratic wallet/batch integration and HTLC witness/proving remain unfinished.
Private wallet worker transport/admission is not implemented; public recursive worker assignments reject this API before private work.
Debug builds perform an explicit CPU constraint audit and reject GPU-required wallet requests before private work.
Static public AIR metadata, entropy acquisition, orchestration, public/proof serialization and independent verification remain host work.
Single-AIR periodic lowering currently excludes committed preprocessing and lookup arguments. Owned multi-AIR commitment remains unfinished.
Full-size wrap/pair/merge/finalizer workloads, production resource calibration, sustained multi-worker throughput and AMD/Metal qualification remain open.
Pending Apple source still requires its authorized local Mac checkpoint commit; no SSH attempted.
